candidates.title: Experts Exhibit Structured Redundancy: Structure-Preserving Expert Pruning for Mixture-of-Experts Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Sparse MoE mechanism significantly improves the trade-off between model capacity and inference efficiency. However, practical deployment still requires storing all experts, resulting in substantial memory overhead. We show that expert outputs in MoE layers exhibit structured redundancy. Across different models and task categories, the stable rank and entropy effective rank of expert outputs are consistently far below the nominal number of experts, while expert output distributions also exhibit fewer effective modes. Motivated by these observations, we reformulate expert pruning as a structure-preserving expert subset selection problem and efficiently optimize it via a greedy strategy, rather than only independently scoring and ranking individual experts or exhaustively searching over expert combinations. We propose two expert pruning methods under the unified structure-preserving framework: Projection Energy Expert Pruning (PEEP), which preserves the functional subspace by maximizing weighted projection energy, and Distributional Coverage Expert Pruning (DCEP), which preserves the distributional geometry by minimizing weighted coverage error. Both methods incorporate router-derived weights as priors, enabling them to jointly preserve the global structural relationships among experts while accounting for the local importance of individual experts. Experiments on DeepSeek-V2-Lite and Qwen3-30B-A3B demonstrate that, at the expert retention ratios of 75% and 50%, our methods outperform the state-of-the-art baselines on the majority of benchmarks and consistently achieve the best average performance across both general tasks and mathematical reasoning tasks.
candidates.reason: MoE expert出力の低いeffective rankと分布modeの重複を利用し、router重みを事前重要度として使いながらexpert集合全体の構造を保つgreedy pruningを提案。PEEPは重み付き射影energy、DCEPは分布coverage誤差を基準とする。DeepSeek-V2-LiteとQwen3-30B-A3Bでexpert保持率75%/50%の比較において多数のbenchmarkで既存pruning法を上回り平均性能が最良と報告。推論常駐expertメモリ削減の直接手法。

candidates.title: SACQ: Structure-Aware Codebook Quantization for Ultra-Low-Bit Vision-Language-Action Models
candidates.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models enable capable robot behavior, but their large memory footprint limits deployment on resource-constrained robotic platforms. Weight quantization is a natural remedy, yet post-training quantization (PTQ) recipes inherited from large language models degrade when applied to VLAs at ultra-low precision. Existing low-bit PTQ methods often fail to explicitly account for the structure of downstream operations and allocate precision without considering its effect on the policy actions. We introduce SACQ, an ultra- low-bit weight-only vector-codebook quantization framework for VLAs. SACQ combines (1) structure-aware codebook fitting with role-specific quadratic metrics that reflect input statistics and downstream sensitivity; (2) action-aware mixed-bit allocation based on the increase in final-action error as individual layers are compressed; and (3) two-stage post-quantization refinement that reassigns codeword indices with second-order error compensation and calibrates codebooks and row-group scales against the decoded action. Using GR00T N1.7, SACQ achieves 93.85% average success across four LIBERO suites at 1.5 bits per language/action weight while reducing model memory by 4.83x. With INT8 activation quantization and low-precision attention, it retains 93.55% success while running 1.51x faster than BF16. On SimplER, SACQ further achieves 63.76% and 52.27% success under Visual Matching and Variant Aggregation at 2 bits per language/action weight, compared to 58.90% and 53.45% for BF16, respectively.
candidates.reason: VLAモデルの言語・行動重みに対し、演算の役割と入力統計を反映したcodebook適合、最終行動誤差による層別混合bit配分、二段階の量子化後補正を組み合わせる。GR00T N1.7で1.5bit時にLIBERO平均成功率93.85%とモデルメモリ4.83倍削減、INT8活性化と低精度attention併用時にBF16比1.51倍高速を報告。ロボットVLA用途だが言語系重みの推論量子化・メモリ/速度改善を直接評価するためaccept。

candidates.title: SparseGDN: Chunk Sparse in Linear Attention
candidates.abstract: Gated Delta Networks (GDNs) offer linear-time sequence modeling, yet long-context prefill remains costly due to dense intra-chunk computation, recurrent-state updates, and intermediate state storage. We introduce SparseGDN, a hardware-aware framework that combines structured intra-chunk approximation with input-dependent recurrent-event selection while producing outputs for every token. A block-adjacent solver reduces local Delta-solve computation, while a dynamic selector allocates recurrent-update budgets across head pairs. The GPU implementation materializes updates only for selected events and reconstructs token outputs using compact state snapshots and group-local interactions, reducing computation and memory traffic. We evaluate SparseGDN on Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.5-9B across RULER tasks and context lengths from 4K to 128K. Retaining approximately 29% of recurrent events on average, SparseGDN achieves 1.50-1.94x GDN-core prefill speedups over native FLA kernels, including online selection overhead.
candidates.reason: Gated Delta Networksの長文prefillで、chunk内の密なDelta solveとrecurrent state更新が律速になる問題に対し、隣接block solverと入力依存の更新イベント選択を組み合わせる。Qwen3.5-4B/9B、4K〜128K文脈のRULER評価で平均約29%のrecurrent eventを残し、選択器の費用込みでnative FLA比1.50〜1.94倍のGDN core prefill高速化を報告。LLM推論カーネルと状態メモリの直接最適化。

candidates.title: There Is No Free Loop: When Does Looping a Trained Model Pay for Its Inference Compute?
candidates.abstract: Looping re-applies a block of layers so that each token passes through the block more than once. Adding a loop to a trained model is attractive because it leaves the parameter count, and hence the disk size, the memory footprint and the training cost unchanged. Unfortunately, every generated token pays for the loop. Re-applying m of N layers makes each token about (N+m)/N times as expensive. Loops that a model learns during large-scale pretraining justify this price, but whether loops added after pretraining justify this cost remains unclear. We compare a looped model with two simple baselines. We first compare it with the same model trained identically without the loop (equal parameters). Secondly, we compare it with the best unlooped use of the same inference floating-point operations (equal FLOPs). Across Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 models from 0.8B to 9B parameters, only the looped 0.8B model beats both baselines. At 4B and 9B, the looped model does not beat the first baseline, i.e. the same model trained without the loop. This is not because the benchmarks are too easy, since on the same benchmarks the unlooped 9B model still scores up to 13 points higher than the 4B model, showing that there is ample room for improvement. Introducing loops in an already pretrained model therefore only pays for small models with a fixed parameter budget.
candidates.reason: 学習済みLLMへ重み共有loopを追加するとパラメータ・保存サイズは増えない一方、生成token当たり計算量は追加層mと元層Nに応じて約(N+m)/N倍となる。この費用を同パラメータと同推論FLOPsの2基準でQwen3/Qwen3.5の0.8B〜9Bに比較し、両基準を上回ったのは0.8Bだけ、4B/9Bは非loopの同学習モデルに勝てないと報告。推論計算予算に対する構造選択の負の実証結果として直接有用。
